title: Joining Words with 'And'
keyIdea: 'And' is a joining word (a conjunction). It goes between two things to join them: cats and dogs. It can join two sentences into one longer sentence: 'The dog barked and the cat ran.' The full stop in the middle goes, and the second part starts with a small letter, except 'I' and names. In a list of three or more things, commas go between the things and 'and' goes only before the last one: a hat, a coat and a scarf. 'And' joins ideas that go together, and a long chain of ands is hard to follow, so start a new sentence instead.

kid: 'And' is a joining word. It joins two things. I like cats and dogs. 'And' goes in the middle, between the two things.
'And' can join two sentences. The dog barked. The cat ran. Now make one: The dog barked and the cat ran. One sentence has one full stop, at the end.
In a list, put a comma between the things. Put 'and' just before the last one. I packed a hat, a coat and a scarf.
Join ideas that go together. I was cold and I put on my coat. Do not use too many ands. If it gets long, stop and start a new sentence.
adult: The English national curriculum (Appendix 2) asks Year 1 pupils to join words and join clauses using 'and'. Their terms are word, sentence, full stop and capital letter. Year 2 adds co-ordination with 'or', 'and' and 'but', and commas to separate items in a list, with the terms statement and comma. The word conjunction is a pupil term from Year 3. Before that, 'joining word' is the usual name.

'And' is a co-ordinating conjunction. It links two words, two phrases or two main clauses of equal weight. When two sentences become one, the first full stop goes. The next word loses its capital letter, unless it is 'I' or a name. In a list of three or more things, school style puts commas between the items and 'and' before the last one. A comma before that last 'and' (the Oxford comma) is optional.

Common mistakes: putting 'and' before both items or at the end ('and cats dogs'); leaving the first full stop in ('I ran. and I jumped'); writing a small 'i' in the middle; using 'and' between every item in a list; joining ideas with no link; and the very common chain of 'and then… and then… and then', where one sentence runs on and on.

In the lab your child drags 'and' between two things and joins two sentences, then sees the full stop go. They build lists with a comma and an 'and', and pick the idea that fits after 'and'. Last, they tap extra ands to turn a long chain into short sentences.

familyTip: Tell each other about your day in two short sentences, then join them with 'and'. When a story turns into 'and then… and then…', clap where a new sentence should start.

visual.caption: Is 'and' used the right way? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: We swam and we had chips.
We swam. and we had chips.
I see a cat, a dog and a hen.
I see a cat and, a dog a hen.
It rained and we got wet.
It rained and my pen is red.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: put 'and' between two things, join two sentences, build lists, pick ideas that go together and break up a chain of ands.

practice.prompt: Where does 'and' go? I like ___ apples ___ pears ___.
choices: I like apples and pears.
I like and apples pears.
I like apples pears and.
practice.hint: 'And' joins two things. Put it between them.
practice.explain: 'And' sits between the two things it joins: apples and pears.

practice.prompt: Zara joins {n} pairs of short sentences with 'and'. Each pair becomes one sentence. How many full stops are there now?
practice.hint: Each joined sentence has one full stop, at the end.
practice.explain: Each pair becomes one sentence with one full stop, so {n} pairs make {n} sentences and {n} full stops.

practice.prompt: Join 'The sun came out.' and 'We went to the park.'
choices: The sun came out and we went to the park.
The sun came out. and we went to the park.
The sun came and out we went to the park.
practice.hint: Take out the first full stop. Put 'and' where it was.
practice.explain: The first full stop goes, 'and' joins the two ideas, and 'We' becomes 'we' because it is not the start any more.

practice.prompt: A list has {n} things in it. How many commas does it need, with 'and' before the last thing?
practice.hint: Count the gaps between things. The last gap gets 'and', not a comma.
practice.explain: {n} things have {=n-1} gaps. The last gap gets 'and', so {=n-2} gaps get a comma.

choices: It joins words and ideas
It ends a sentence
It asks a question
pool.hint: Think of 'cats and dogs'. What does 'and' do there?
pool.explain: 'And' is a joining word, a conjunction. It joins two things or two ideas.

pool.prompt: Which list is written the right way?
choices: I ate eggs, toast and jam.
I ate eggs and toast and and jam.
I ate eggs, toast, jam and.
pool.hint: Commas between things. 'And' just before the last one.
pool.explain: Eggs, toast and jam: a comma between the first two, and 'and' before the last thing.

pool.prompt: Join 'I got up.' and 'I had my breakfast.'
choices: I got up and I had my breakfast.
I got up and i had my breakfast.
I got up. And I had my breakfast and.
pool.hint: Does 'I' ever get a small letter?
pool.explain: One full stop at the end, and 'I' always keeps its capital letter, even in the middle.

choices: I was hungry and I ate a sandwich.
I was hungry and the sky is blue.
I was hungry and the car is fast.
pool.hint: Does the second idea have something to do with the first?
pool.explain: Being hungry and eating a sandwich go together. The other endings have nothing to do with being hungry.

choices: We went to the zoo. We saw a lion and it roared.
We went to the zoo and we saw a lion and it roared and we went home and we slept.
We went to the zoo we saw a lion it roared.
pool.hint: Look for short sentences with a full stop at the end of each.
pool.explain: Too many ands make one long chain. Short sentences, with one 'and' at most, are easy to follow.

pool.prompt: A sentence has {n} ands in a long chain. You change all but one of them into full stops. How many ands are left?
pool.hint: All but one means you keep just one.
pool.explain: You change {=n-1} of the {n} ands into full stops, so 1 'and' is left.

pool.prompt: You write {n} short sentences. Then you join two of them with 'and'. How many sentences are there now?
pool.hint: Two sentences become one, so you have one fewer.
pool.explain: Joining two sentences turns 2 into 1, so {n} sentences become {=n-1}.

pool.prompt: Where does 'and' go in a list of four things?
choices: Just before the last thing
Between every thing
Right at the start
pool.explain: Commas go between the first things, and 'and' goes just before the last one: red, blue, green and pink.
